name: Hydrangea Pink
lede: Hydrangea Pink is named for the flower, a soft pink with a hint of yellow, and for a plant whose color is famously unsteady.

sections.title: The name
sections.body: Paterson defines hydrangea pink as a yellowy pink, and notes the same flower also lends the names hydrangea blue and hydrangea red [1]. It is filed with the pinks, near azalea pink, baby pink and old rose [2].

sections.title: A flower that changes color
sections.body: Jarman remarks that the hydrangea can change its colour from pink to blue and back again [3]. That makes the name a snapshot: any one hydrangea pink is the flower on a particular plant at a particular time [3]. The books examined do not explain the cause, so this article does not either [1][3].

sections.title: Neighbors
sections.body: Near relatives in our list are [[baby-pink]], [[blush-pink]] and [[pink]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #E1C1BA measures lightness 80.6, chroma 12.8 and hue angle 37 degrees: a pale, quiet pink leaning a little toward orange, which matches the dictionary's wording of yellowy pink [1][4].
